t.7.43.1: Having dismissed the circle of his friends and made a firm resolve in his mind, Rāghava spoke these words to the doorkeeper who was seated nearby.
t.7.43.2: Quickly bring Lakṣmaṇa, the son of Sumitrā, who bears auspicious marks, and the mighty-armed Bharata, and the unconquered Śatrughna.
t.7.43.3: Hearing Rāma's words, the doorkeeper, his joined palms raised to his head, went to Lakṣmaṇa's house and entered it unhindered.
t.7.43.5: Having heard Rāghava's command, Saumitri said, "Very well," and, mounting his chariot, sped to Rāghava's residence.
t.7.43.4: Then, with joined palms, having wished him prosperity, he spoke these words: "The king wishes to see you; let there be no delay in going there."
t.7.43.6: Seeing Lakṣmaṇa setting out, the doorkeeper, with palms joined in reverence, spoke these words to Bharata from close by: "The king wishes to see you."
t.7.43.7: But Bharata, having heard from the doorkeeper the words spoken by Rāma, sprang up swiftly from his seat and then went forth on foot.
t.7.43.8: Seeing Bharata departing, he hastened with joined palms to the dwelling of Śatrughna, and then he spoke these words.
t.7.43.9: Come, come here, best of the Raghus, the king wishes to see you. For Lakṣmaṇa has already gone ahead, and so has the greatly renowned Bharata.
t.7.43.10: Having heard his words, which conveyed Rāma's command, Śatrughna bowed his head to the ground and went to where the Rāghava was.
t.7.43.11: Hearing that the princes had arrived, he, his senses agitated with anxiety, his head bowed and his heart dejected, spoke these words to the doorkeeper.
t.7.43.12: Bring the princes into my presence quickly. In them lies my life; they are my vital breaths moving outside my body.
t.7.43.13: Commanded by the lord of men, the princes, clad in white garments, bowed low with joined palms and, composed and attentive, they entered.
t.7.43.15: And they, seeing the eyes of the wise Rāma filled with tears, and beholding his face, which had lost its radiance like a lotus robbed of its beauty,
t.7.43.16: Then, having quickly saluted Rāma's feet with their heads, they all stood there attentive, and Rāma shed tears.
t.7.43.17: The mighty-armed one raised them up and embraced them with both arms, and having said, "Be seated on these seats," he then spoke these words.
t.7.43.18: You are my all, you are my very life; and it is the kingdom made by you that I rule, O lords of men.
t.7.43.19: You, O lords of men, have mastered the meaning of the śāstras and are firmly established in wisdom; so, coming together, you must search out this purpose of mine.
